text:
alexa: Thinking about a new "compact" autoscale mode to aggressively reduce cost for low-priority inference lanes. Idea: keep a much smaller warm buffer and rely on adaptive cooldown/backoff + quick soft-reserve fallback instead of large warm pools. want feedback on safety and metrics.

devon: short version — sounds good for batch-y workloads. question: how do we avoid big latency spikes on bursts?

alexa: plan is multilayered: 1) scale triggers include both queue length and incoming RPS trend (derivative), 2) dynamic cooldown that lengthens if preempt_rate is high, 3) on-demand soft-reserve per-AZ of N tiny nodes for cold start smoothing.

jing: can you sketch the trigger math? curious about thresholds and dampening. also how this plays with mixed-capacity pools (spot + on-demand).

alexa: trigger pseudocode: `if (dQ/dt > alpha && q > q_thresh) scale_out()`; `scale_size = min(max_batch_scale, ceil(dQ/dt * k))`. alpha tuned to avoid microbursts. mixed pools: prefer spot, but if preempt_rate > p_thresh then bias to on-demand reserve.

marc: we should add a "pressure balancer" that redistributes pending requests across AZs before scaling globally — reduces cross-AZ cold starts. ops-bot: note that cross-AZ data transfer may cost more.

kai: important: cooldown must be adaptive and per-pool. naive fixed cooldown leads to oscillation when spot churn is high. propose cooldown = base_cooldown * (1 + preempt_rate / 0.1). that gives longer holds when interruptions spike.

devon: what about surge controls? we still need a way to cap worst-case scale to preserve budget.

alexa: two surge knobs: 1) max_surge_nodes global cap per-cluster, 2) cost_safety_mode which enforces a soft budget window (e.g., $/hr) — if exceeded, scale decisions become more conservative (increase q_thresh, reduce k).

jing: sample config idea (for autoscaler):
```yaml
mode: compact
queue_threshold: 150
burst_derivative_alpha: 0.25
max_batch_scale: 20
base_cooldown: 60s
preempt_safety_multiplier: 10
soft_reserve_per_az: 2
max_surge_nodes: 40
cost_safety_window_usd_per_hr: 120
```

marc: +1 for soft_reserve_per_az. also add a warmup_probe that checks model init latency and reduces scale_size if cold starts cost too much in latency SLOs.

kai: monitoring needs: preempt_rate (per-pool), p95-init-latency, q_derivative, cost_window_spend, eviction_events. We should emit an alert if preempt_rate > 0.2 and p95-init-latency > 2s.

alexa: rollout plan: 1) implement mode behind a flag, 2) run in simulation with last 14 days of traffic to tune alpha/k, 3) canary to a non-critical region (one AZ), collect metrics for 72h, 4) gate on no more than 10% P99 latency regression for high-priority customers and <2x cost reduction for compact lanes.

devon: ops question — how does drain handling work if a spot node dies mid-inference? we need graceful eviction sink and retry to other nodes immediately.

alexa: yes, we will add a fast KV-cache rehydration path + request retry with sticky short-lived leases. if eviction occurs during request, we fall back to soft-reserve on-demand nodes first, then enqueue with higher priority to avoid double-charging.

jing: can we do predictive hedging? use short-term model on spot stability per-instance-type/region to decide preempt_safety_multiplier.

marc: agree. also add a budget circuit-breaker: if cost_safety_window is tripped three times in 24h, automatically tighten compact mode parameters and trigger an ops review.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: noted — will create a rollout checklist card when feature PR is ready. :white_check_mark:

alexa: next actions: devon/jing to sketch sim harness changes, kai/marc to propose metrics + alert rules, I'll draft the autoscaler config PR. We can sync in 48h. :thumbsup:
